text: The plan status reaches rwb-case from rwb-integration one case at a time: the plan-status step of DailyCaseRun calls GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status inside the readPlanStatus activity, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream, and the page size of the case page bounds the concurrency, so no batch form of the read is built
why: No source gives a hand-over between rwb-integration and rwb-case for this legacy key: the Architecture v5 connection matrix has neither a P3 to P2 call nor a P2 to P3 call, the legacy in-process call read the plan inside the same service and only assumed batches of 500 (DL11)
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13, slide 14 and slide 16; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-11; legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 3 and section 12
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 3, section 12.2 and section 13
confirm: Solution architect confirms the direction of the hand-over and the batching rule in the rwb-integration contract story
impact: The daily step is built and tested against the rwb-integration contract fake on Day 1; a batch operation later changes the client only, not the step

text: The catalog row of a fired rule is read through the rwb-decision contract by rule ID and package version; until the P7 catalog read is published, the story reads it through the P7 contract fake and takes action_text, owner_role and timer_spec from the evaluated row
why: The Ownership Map puts rule_row, rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_test_case in rwb-decision (P7), and the route move needs the action text, the owner role and the timer spec, but no published P7 operation reads a catalog row
read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 T6; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_row); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 4 step 9, section 11 and section 12.2
confirm: P7 decision owner publishes the catalog-row read in the rwb-decision contract story
impact: The move can be built and tested against the fake; when the P7 contract lands only the client path changes

text: The plan event map is loaded as versioned reference data of rwb-case under a table code added to LOV-REF-TABLE, one reference_row per ACE status and route state pair, and no map row sits in code
why: The legacy story keeps the map as a versioned reference table, and the target reference_version and reference_row are keyed by a table code that LOV-REF-TABLE does not list for this map
read: TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.2 LOV-REF-TABLE and T3.1 reference_version and reference_row; legacy RWB-E2-002 section 3 and section 13
confirm: Reference data owner (RW-COE) and the rwb-case reference-data story add the table code and load the rows
impact: The event codes of AC2 and AC10 are read from rows either way; loading the code is a data change, not a code change

text: A missing plan status and an unknown status code are recorded in the run summary of DailyCaseRun and listed from there for the data steward and the ACE team; rwb-case writes no break row until rwb-source-data publishes a break operation
why: reconciliation_result is owned by rwb-source-data under the Ownership Map and no operation lets rwb-case raise a break, while the legacy story wrote the break from inside the monolith
read: FSD P3 Case and workflow v4 A2.28 AC-EXC-P3-028-01; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (reconciliation_result); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2002-APP section 5 X1 and X3, and section 13
confirm: P1 source data owner publishes the break operation in the rwb-source-data contract story
impact: No build block: the exceptions are still named, counted and listed; only the persisted break row is deferred

text: The plan section of the case record is served by a gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case and rwb-integration in parallel, one hop each, shows the live answer when it is present and the stored answer with MSG-P2-008 when it is not; the route path, the merge order and the field masking are agreed in RWB-PLT-N001-CON
why: Architecture v5 fixes the parallel composite pattern and a 2 s budget but gives no route, no merge rule and no masking rule for this screen
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 and slide 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19; legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 8 and section 15
confirm: Solution architect confirms the composite route in the gateway-bff contract story
impact: The panel is built and tested against a route fake; the screen goes live with the edge story

text: rwb-case connects with one login of its own that holds rights in schema rwb_case only, and the name, the grants and the secret reference are agreed in the database story of the epic; the story names it 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' until then
why: Template and Rules v1 section R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service but no source gives the name, the grant set or the secret reference
read: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 and slide 41; TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.5
confirm: ACE database administrator confirms the login name and its grants
impact: No build block: the login is a secret reference and a grant script; the name is filled in when the database story lands
